decision_question.question: Should the existing June 14 Phase 3A snapshot remain the strict historical whole-source gate, should a separately ratified snapshot epoch replace it after dual-run migration, or should a new supported-entrypoint gate be introduced while retaining the June snapshot as migration evidence?
decision_question.governance_boundary: The additive Core CAS API release is a separate compatibility decision. It neither authorizes replacing the Phase 3A baseline nor proves that the historical snapshot is a complete model of supported public API.

rationale: The accepted Phase 3A plan defines a fail-closed pre-decomposition snapshot and requires the gate green before Phase 5/6. Replacing its June baseline with current output would move the reference point across a broad, not-yet-owner-adjudicated delta.

The gate walks all source modules, including modules that the separate public-surface contract treats as internal unless listed. The current inventory cannot yet resolve the Core artifacts facade exports, so switching the historical gate to that inventory would substitute an incomplete source of truth.

The CAS feature is an additive API on an already supported public_stable entrypoint. It can follow the existing release-fragment and inventory-review path without rewriting the historical Phase 3A baseline.
recommended_decision.immediate_effect: Keep architecture/baselines/structure_remediation/public_surface_pre_decomp.json and the whole-source Phase 3A comparator byte-for-byte unchanged. Do not claim the gate green: the audit observed nonzero normalized snapshot differences, but the candidate audit did not execute pytest.
recommended_decision.authority: Only team-architecture can accept a change to the Phase 3A gate/baseline scope. team-polisyos owns the additive Core API release classification. The candidate author has no authority to ratify either decision.
recommended_decision.time_and_status: The baseline timestamp (2026-06-14T06:21:47.482093+00:00) is historical provenance, not an expiry, automatic renewal, or waiver. The current decision remains HOLD for global baseline/scope change; runtime tests and generators remain UNRUN in the supplied audit.
recommended_decision.p41: not_established: the exact pre-slice base was not replayed with a zero intersection against the full source-file denominator. Do not attribute the delta to inherited debt or to the additive CAS feature.

decision_options.semantics: Keep the June 14 v1 full-source baseline and fail-closed equality gate as the Phase 3A migration fence. Any proposed update must be an explicit, owner-reviewed successor; do not refresh the baseline as a side effect of this API addition.
decision_options.benefit: Preserves the accepted pre-decomposition record and the phase-entry control already named by the accepted plan.
decision_options.cost_or_limit: The recorded broad delta remains unresolved and the gate cannot be represented as green from this audit. This does not classify every difference as a supported public API change.
decision_options.migration: No global migration. Continue to retain the v1 artifact and review the full delta. Address the additive CAS surface through its own release fragment and reviewed inventory.

decision_options.semantics: Define a separately versioned successor snapshot with an explicit, owner-approved property/schema and a baseline frozen from a reviewed candidate. Keep v1 readable and run both gates during a declared transition.
decision_options.benefit: Makes any new scope and newly represented fields explicit, rather than silently changing the meaning of the June artifact.
decision_options.cost_or_limit: Requires team-architecture to accept the new epoch and a complete baseline transition; the broad current delta cannot be wholesale blessed by choosing a new version. The v1 gate remains a phase criterion until the accepted migration says otherwise.
decision_options.migration: Specify schema and source boundary, freeze exact source and generator identities, review every delta, dual-run v1 and v2, then separately record when v1 ceases to be a blocking phase gate. Preserve v1 bytes as historical evidence.

decision_options.semantics: Keep the June v1 snapshot as a historical migration audit while adding a distinct gate whose scope follows the supported-entrypoint contract and whose export set is derived from a complete, fail-closed source of truth.
decision_options.benefit: Separates public compatibility from internal-module restructuring and can align the live gate with the stated internal-by-default rule.
decision_options.cost_or_limit: The current generated inventory is unresolved for polisyos.core.artifacts; its 89 candidate names (and any regenerated 92 source candidates) are not runtime-export proof. It cannot presently serve as the complete gate basis. Existing direct imports and external compatibility obligations still need owner review.
decision_options.migration: First make export resolution complete or explicitly fail closed on unresolved exports, prove supported-entrypoint coverage and negatives, run the new gate alongside v1, and obtain team-architecture approval before changing Phase 5/6 gate requirements. Do not treat this as acceptance of the historical delta.
